record.statement: theorem full_support (W : BrownianSystem Ω) (γ : OrderParameter) (hmin : IsMinimizer W γ) : FullSupportConclusion W γ
record.boundary: Pure zero-field SK with covariance normalization xi(t)=t^2/2. Conditional on the supplied order parameter being an admissible integrable minimizer; no separate assertion that a minimizer exists. FullSupportConclusion includes Stieltjes-measure and diffusion existence, full relative support, strict increase, and the two selected diffusion moment identities. It does not assert QAOA circuit-energy convergence.

aligned_passages.text:
### 12.1 The support statement and the derivative bridge

The first formal statement assumes a Brownian system and an admissible
minimizer. It supplies a Stieltjes measure, an associated diffusion, full
relative support and strict increase, and the two moment identities for
every associated diffusion. Its proof assembles contact, exclusion of a
terminal plateau, curvature for positive and zero constant intervals,
and uniqueness to transfer the moments between associated diffusions.
This describes the inspected proof's mathematical route; no successful
research-target replay is claimed. Its quantifiers are
$\forall W\,\forall\gamma$, followed by the minimizer hypothesis;
it supplies both witnesses on the given Brownian system. The moment
conclusion is universal over every diffusion satisfying the specified
equation, and covers exactly $0\le t<1$. The diffusion equation itself
holds through time one, simultaneously for all those times outside
one null set. Controls are progressive for the natural filtration of
Brownian increments and bounded by one pointwise. These are not
additional regularity or minimizer-existence assumptions. See the
[exact support statement][support-type] and the companion
source-interface review.

There is one useful distinction between the manuscript's first variation
and its formal counterpart. The formal result initially gives a derivative
along chord lengths $1/(n+1)$. For this particular control functional,
that sampled limit determines the ordinary feasible right derivative.
With a control fixed, the terminal absolute value is convex in the
coefficient while the penalty is linear. The supremum over the same
control class, and then subtraction of the linear Parisi penalty,
preserve convexity. The secant slopes therefore vary monotonically as
the chord shortens; each intervening chord lies between two successive
sampled chords and has the same limiting slope. If $\eta$ is an
integrable feasible direction, choose $\varepsilon_0>0$ so that
$\gamma+\varepsilon_0\eta$ is admissible and rescale the chord. This
bridge is an ordinary deduction from the definitions and sampled limit,
not an additional formally named theorem.

At the origin, the manuscript smoothly extends auxiliary quotient
variables. The formal coercivity proof for the spatial diffusion density instead works on the positive
half-line, controls the zero flux at the origin and reflects. What must
agree is the resulting integrated inequality; auxiliary values at zero
need not coincide. In particular, the declared generic flux lemma has
a global derivative hypothesis that is not the supplier used here:
the finite-density proof uses the Gaussian half-line coercivity lemma
and reflection. A totalized quotient value at zero cannot silently
satisfy the generic global hypothesis. The precise source spans are in
the correspondence record.
The [fixed-time supplier `actual_coercivity`][support-fixed-time] assumes
positive time and continuity of the coefficient at that time. Its scaled
polynomial inequality is (4.1) multiplied by $c^2$; division requires
$c>0$. This gives a direct source destination for Proposition 4.1 without
adding a minimizing or plateau premise.

The source collection retains the two manuscripts, formal statements,
their implementations and build metadata. The derived project specifies
Lean 4.34.1 and a pinned mathlib revision. The proof-assistant and library
infrastructure is described by [de Moura and Ullrich (2021), *The Lean 4
Theorem Prover and Programming Language*](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-79876-5_37)
and [The mathlib Community (2020), *The Lean Mathematical Library*](https://doi.org/10.1145/3372885.3373824).
These references credit the software; the retained project metadata identifies
the versions used for this source. The retained polynomial computation
in §4 uses exact rational arithmetic. Its expansion matches
all 22 positive remainder
coefficients. The surplus of the $v^4$ coefficient above $1/1000$ is
$140507/1521000000$. This finite check does not establish the PDE
signs, integrability, boundary flux or limiting argument.

The source-byte audit verified the inspected edition; it did not prove
its claims. Paper assembly checked identifiers, declared scope and
document bindings, not semantic correspondence or reader understanding.
Tool-compatibility checks and synthetic fixtures exercised their stated
cases, not either selected SK theorem. Reading of the mathematical and
formal sources supports the bounded comparisons reported here, without
a complete independent proof acceptance or transitive axiom audit.

The retained observations must be kept separate. The original graph records
unrun plans and an earlier full-support attempt that could not start
because the Comparator executable was unavailable. A later retained
attempt, observed on 23 October 2026, built and exported the challenge,
then stopped while building the implementing solution. The retained
partial-observation receipt and log preserve that event: the imported
object for `Diffusion/AbsIncrement` was missing. The challenge is an
admitted specification, so its successful build and export are not a
proof of the theorem. There was no successful solution export or
research-target comparison in that observation.

The scalar-value invocation in the same original two-target run reached
a terminal failure observed on 24 October 2026. Its challenge built and
exported, but its solution build stopped because the imported object for
`Gaussian/IntegralPositiveMulGaussian` was missing. The retained scalar
receipt and log establish no solution export, kernel acceptance or
comparison acceptance. The companion source review locates both records.
Both failures concern the original build configuration. A subsequent
repair to the derived configuration was recorded. In the subsequent
corrected replay, the full-support challenge built and its exporter was
observed running. Reconciliation on 25 October found that the controller
had stopped without a recovered terminal research result. Comparator
and research extraction outcomes therefore remain unknown, neither
rejected nor accepted. The companion source review retains this
interruption separately from the original build failures.

The later observation is additional run history, not a replacement for
the earlier event or a mathematical rejection of the theorem. Neither
research target has a successful source-bound comparison and transitive
axiom audit established here. Permitted axioms and checker settings
describe configuration; source names and tool-fixture receipts cannot
supply the missing target result. The full-support receipt remains a
historical partial observation; the scalar receipt is a terminal failure
of its original invocation. Neither is a replay of the subsequently
repaired source configuration.

This editorial revision does not establish a new formal result.
Detailed reading coverage, exact finite-check
results, preserved unsuccessful observations and the remaining obligations
are recorded in the companion source review. This remains a draft after source-based agent review; independent mathematical acceptance and a human reconstruction study have not been performed.

This AI-assisted article reconstructs the cited analytic arguments. The integrated estimate (5), its shape hypotheses and compact-strip approximation are substantial imported inputs. The [full-support formal statement][support-challenge] asserts the support and moment conclusions conditional on an admissible minimiser, and constructs its associated diffusion. A separate [scalar formal statement][value-challenge] covers value identities and finite Gaussian approximation, with minimiser and diffusion premises for those clauses. Its third clause identifies the ground-state and Parisi values from a minimiser, constructing the diffusion internally. The two formal models have not been transported into one another in this record. Neither statement includes the positive-density corollary or QAOA convergence. Their [full-support][support-lean] and [scalar][value-lean] implementations use [Lean][Lean4] and [mathlib][mathlib]. Acceptance by Comparator and extraction of the selected formal statements remain unknown. Source inspection alone establishes neither. Exact versions, checking outcomes and correspondence are retained in the long record's [§12, “What the formal statements establish”](../long/reasoning-record.md#formal-interfaces) and [§13, “Source checks and finite calculation”](../long/reasoning-record.md#verification).

## Sources and scope of verification This account reconstructs selected parts of OpenAI's analytic manuscript. The global scaling argument for contact follows Chen's variational proof; the terminal convexity argument in Section 5.4 is an ordinary deduction from the stated curvature, contact and boundedness inputs. It is not a claim that this alternative proof has been replayed in Lean. The Lean [implementation][support-proof], [challenge statement][support-interface] and [Comparator configuration][support-config] concern a minimiser's support and moment identities. They assume a minimiser; they do not prove the external Parisi formula or attainment. The separate scalar [implementation][value-proof] and [statement][value-interface] concern the value identity and finite Gaussian approximation. Neither selected statement covers positive density, the external near-ground overlap theorem used in Section 6, or the complete QAOA circuit theorem. The implementations use [Lean 4 (de Moura–Ullrich, 2021)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-79876-5_37) and [mathlib (The mathlib Community, 2020)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3372885.3373824). Comparator acceptance and research-v2 extraction remain unknown; see the *Long Reasoning Record*, [§13](../long/reasoning-record.md#verification). Kernel checking establishes a declared statement under its definitions and axioms. Its correspondence with the analytic theorem, independent proof review and reader comprehension are separate questions. The links below select the editions used. - **OpenAI (2026a).** *Full support of the zero-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick order parameter*, 27 September 2026. [Pinned manuscript][support-manuscript]. §2 supplies regularity, Proposition 5.1 the strict curvature estimate, §6 the support proof, and Corollary 6.4 the additional density conclusion. - **Hong-Bin Chen (2026).** *FRSB in the SK spin glass: convergence to full-interval support at zero temperature*. [Version 1][chen-support], Theorem 1.3 for earlier full support and smooth nonnegative density; Proposition 3.2 for contact by scaling the coefficient. Strictly positive density in the further-reading note uses the separate OpenAI corollary. - **Antonio Auffinger and Wei-Kuo Chen (2017).** *Parisi formula for the ground state energy in the mixed p-spin model*, Annals of Probability 45(6B), 4617–4631. [Version 2][auffinger-chen]. The variational formula and attainment used in Section 3.2. - **Aukosh Jagannath and Ian Tobasco (2016).** *A dynamic programming approach to the Parisi functional*, Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society 144, 3135–3150. [Version 4][jt-control]. The control method, with finite-temperature terminal data; it is not by itself the zero-temperature regularity theorem used here. - **Wei-Kuo Chen, Madeline Handschy and Gilad Lerman (2018).** *On the energy landscape of the mixed even p-spin model*, Probability Theory and Related Fields 171, 53–95. [Version 4][chl-optimality]. Proposition 4 gives the first-variation formula used in Section 5.1; the proof of Theorem 6 gives the zero-candidate descent. - **Antonio Auffinger, Wei-Kuo Chen and Qiang Zeng (2020).** *The SK model is infinite step replica symmetry breaking at zero temperature*. [Version 2][acz], Proposition 1 and Remark 7. Near-ground overlap pairs and the earlier terminal-plateau observation. - **OpenAI (2026b).** *QAOA attains the SK ground-state energy in the thermodynamic-first limit*, 25 September 2026. [Pinned manuscript][qaoa-manuscript]. The separate circuit theorem. - **Joao Basso, Edward Farhi, Kunal Marwaha, Benjamin Villalonga and Leo Zhou (2022).** *The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm at High Depth for MaxCut on Large-Girth Regular Graphs and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model*. [Full preprint, version 3][bfmvz], §7, equation (7.2). The eventual-optimality conjecture.
